Write to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\problems-finance.md; return a concise summary. No installs, no MCP, no personal contact data.

Find the 4-6 BIGGEST problems in FINANCIAL SERVICES / INSURANCE / CAPITAL MARKETS / FINTECH BACK-OFFICE that are (1) SOFTWARE-SOLVABLE (no hardware/physical, no field ops), (2) buildable with today's AI/software by a small team on top of frontier models, (3) cost the industry BILLIONS/year (cite the cost), (4) currently UNDER-served (few strong competitors — name the competitors honestly; if crowded, say so), (5) ideally NOT in the most heavily regulated core (flag regulatory load). 
For each problem: the problem, annual cost to the industry (cited), why it's still unsolved, the software approach, who the competitors are (honest), difficulty (easy/med/hard + whether it needs a scientific breakthrough — flag those), rough time-to-MVP, likely acquirers, and a rough value range. Break your top 2 into smaller sub-problems. 
HONESTY: do not invent market sizes or claim "no competition" if there is some; grade weak sources. Flag anything that needs a breakthrough or physical component as OUT of scope. Prefer boring-but-expensive back-office pain over flashy consumer ideas.

handback.t:
Report written to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\problems-finance.md. Read-only desk research; no installs and no personal contact data used. The 200-search budget ran out mid-research, so a few claims are unverified and flagged in the file.

**Ranked shortlist.** None needs a scientific breakthrough (all are LLM extraction plus rules and workflow with human review). None has "no competition". Grades are A primary, B trade press or vendor-sponsored survey, C aggregator or vendor blog.

1. **P&C subrogation and recovery execution (top pick).**
   - Cost: about $15-20B/yr of missed recoveries. That figure is grade C: a SubroIQ vendor blog (2025-04) plus an aggregator attributing it to the NAIC, which I could not verify because the NAIC PDF would not parse. Context: carriers recovered $51.6B in 2021 (NAIC journal, 2023, second-hand).
   - Competitors: CLARA Analytics (detection launched 2025-05-07), Verisk Subrogation Analytics, SubroIQ, claims-platform vendors. Detection is contested. The execution layer (evidence package, demand letters, deadline tracking, arbitration filings) looked thin, but I could not check that.
   - Regulatory load: low to moderate. MVP: about 6-10 weeks for a closed-file audit on contingency pricing.
   - Acquirers (my judgment): Guidewire, CCC, Mitchell, Verisk, Sedgwick, Crawford.
   - Value: my arithmetic gives roughly a $110-190M revenue pool across all vendors, on stated assumptions. It is an upper-bound check, not a market size.
   - Sub-problems (7) are broken out in the file.
2. **Withholding-tax reclaim and cross-border tax-relief ops.**
   - Cost: about $16.4B/yr unreclaimed, roughly 20% of reclaimable tax (TaxTec report, 2025-02-26; grade B/C because TaxTec sells reclaim services).
   - Competitors: GlobeTax (founded 1992, claims 7M+ reclaims a year), Broadridge with Xceptor, TaxTec, and custodians' own relief-at-source programs. These are services-heavy incumbents, not software-first.
   - Regulatory load: moderate (tax). MVP: about 3-4 months for 3-5 markets; the long tail of countries is a multi-year grind.
   - Out-of-scope flag: some countries reportedly require wet-ink originals or a local agent. That is general domain knowledge, not verified here.
   - Sub-problems (7) are broken out in the file.
3. **Corporate-actions notice-to-structured data and exceptions.** Cost is about $58B/yr (DTCC, quoted in a 2025 press release; grade A via B). It is crowded: a 24-member consortium (Swift, DTCC, Euroclear, SIX, UBS and others) is building this, so it is a wedge only, aimed at mid-tier managers and administrators.
4. **Delegated-authority bordereaux ingestion (Lloyd's/MGA).** I could not find a credible annual dollar cost, so none is claimed. The exposure base is about £26B of delegated-authority premium at Lloyd's (grade B/C). Competitors are VIPR (reported around 48-50% of Lloyd's managing agents), Noldor, Unitary and Lloyd's own Delegated Data Manager.
5. **Trade-finance letter-of-credit document examination.** Its cost fails the "billions" test on evidence, since the 50-70% discrepancy and per-shipment figures are all vendor claims (grade C). A fragmented field of small AI players exists. It is optional.

**Considered and rejected.**
- AML alert triage: $206.1B/yr compliance spend (LexisNexis, 2023). Crowded and heavily regulated.
- Reconciliation and break resolution: crowded (Duco, SmartStream, Broadridge, Gresham, Trintech, BlackLine) and no annual cost found.
- Payment exception repair: $12.10 per repair, over $50 per failure per Citi. Regulated core with embedded incumbents; the $118.5B figure is unverified.
- Commercial premium leakage: needs proprietary location or imagery data, so it is a data moat rather than pure software.
- Commercial submission-intake AI: crowded and well-funded (Cytora, Sixfold, Federato, Kalepa).

**Recommendation.** Validate the missed-subrogation rate on one real carrier's closed files before building on it. Run withholding tax as a parallel bet after checking the paper-original constraint.

**Gaps.** No verified source for the subrogation dollar figure. No annual cost found for bordereaux, trade finance or reconciliation, and none invented. The file's section 9 lists every gap.
